## What happened

`live-federation-gate.sh` (the WI-261 live 2-peer shared-hive federation smoke gate) banked a plain
`GATE: RED (sidecar-build)` for a run whose *only* failure was `build-desktop-sidecar.sh`'s bounded
`sidecar.lock` acquisition timing out — while a **legitimate, still-running** concurrent release build
(`bin/build-deb-repacked.sh` → `bin/repack-deb-xz.sh`'s `xz -9`, observed running 2419s / 40min) held
the lock. Nothing about the federation smokes was exercised or disproved. See `EI-21164709090643162`.

## The general lesson

**A resource acquisition that times out against a resource *someone else is legitimately using* is
evidence about *contention*, not evidence about whatever the acquisition was supposed to feed into.**
This gate already had several instances of the same underlying principle — `SKIPPED-STORM` (host load
spiked mid-run), `SKIPPED-RIG-BUSY`/`SKIPPED-GATE-IN-FLIGHT` (a shared resource was already claimed),
`SKIPPED-STARVATION` (frame starvation, restart-class unproven) — but the build step had **no such
downgrade path**: `storm_downgrade_eligible()` explicitly refuses to downgrade a `FAIL_BUILD`, so any
lock timeout there fell straight through to a product-looking `RED`, with no way to tell "the fixture
producer collided with another legitimate writer" apart from "the code broke."

When you build (or extend) a gate/CI step that acquires a shared, contended resource before it can
even START producing its evidence (a lock, a port, a display, a rig slot, a database connection pool
slot), ask: **can this acquisition fail for a reason that has nothing to do with what I'm testing?**
If yes, that failure mode needs its own typed disposition (a `SKIPPED-*`/`PARTIAL`-style verdict),
distinguishable from an actual red, so:
- it doesn't file a misleading bug report against the product,
- it doesn't get treated as proof of a regression by anyone reading the verdict,
- but it also **never gets recorded as a green** (nothing was actually proven this window).

## How to detect it safely (the fail-closed rule)

Don't infer contention from a bare timeout alone — a timeout can *also* mean a genuine deadlock/wedge
in the locking code itself, which you very much want to see as a real red. The fix here
(`build_lock_contention_check()` in `live-federation-gate.sh`) requires **both**:
1. the exact diagnostic string the timeout helper emits (`__pc_report_sidecar_lock_timeout()` in
   `bin/lib/sidecar-lock-yield.sh` — pin the regex to the ONE emitter of that exact shape, or it can
   silently stop matching if the message wording drifts), **and**
2. at least one concrete **live holder line** (a real pid + still-running elapsed time + argv) —
   i.e. the diagnostic *proved* a real process still owns the lock.

If the holder details come back "unavailable" (no `fuser`/procps, or the diagnostic couldn't resolve
a pid), that is **not** proof of fair contention — it's an unknown, and the safe default is to leave
it as an ordinary red rather than silently swallow a genuine wedge into a "just contention, ignore it"
bucket. Fail closed toward the more visible outcome when you can't tell the two apart.

## A confusing wrinkle this gate has (worth knowing generally)

`live-federation-gate.sh` self-snapshots to `/tmp` before running (protects a long-running script from
a concurrent in-place edit on the shared tree corrupting its execution mid-run — see the file's own
`GATE_SELF_SNAPSHOT` comment). That means **a fix landing in the tracked file *after* a run's snapshot
was taken has zero effect on that already-in-flight run** — it will keep running the pre-fix behavior
even though `git log`/reading the live file shows the fix already merged. When correlating "why did
this run behave like the old code" against "the fix is right there in the file", check the run's start
timestamp against the fixing commit's timestamp before concluding the fix doesn't work — in this
incident, a run that started at 10:37:41 local hit exactly this: the fix committed at 10:49:05, eleven
minutes later, so that one run's snapshot genuinely predated it. Any other long-running script over
this shared tree that self-snapshots (or doesn't, and is vulnerable to the mid-run edit corruption the
snapshot pattern exists to prevent) shares this property.

## Where the fix lives

`papercusp-desktop/bin/live-federation-gate.sh` — `build_lock_contention_check()` plus the
`GATE: SKIPPED-BUILD-LOCK-CONTENTION` branch inside the `FAIL_BUILD` handling.
Regression tests: `papercusp-desktop/test/live-federation-gate-lock-contention.test.js` (registered in
`test:shell`) — includes an end-to-end recurrence check that genuinely holds a synthetic lock past the
bounded wait with a real live process and feeds the real diagnostic through the real classifier.
